top.name: Nvidia
top.section: Semiconductors: compute, IP and power chips
top.why: Revenue rose +106% and data center +117%, with a 66.2% operating margin and $21.3B of quarterly FCF. Its Q3 guide is $108B. No other company in the set combines growth, margin and cash at this scale.

top.name: TSMC
top.section: Semiconductors: compute, IP and power chips
top.why: Revenue rose +41% in USD, gross profit +69% and operating margin reached 58.7%. Q4 is guided at +58% YoY. It is the leading-edge foundry that every AI chip in this list depends on.

top.name: ASML
top.why: Revenue rose +55% and gross margin widened to 57.5% from 51.6%. Management says supply stays short of demand through 2028. Its EUV monopoly makes it the most durable 15-year asset in semis.

top.name: Broadcom
top.section: Semiconductors: compute, IP and power chips
top.why: Revenue rose +86% and AI semis +221%. FCF was $13.7B, 46% of revenue. VMware is already in the base, so the growth is effectively organic.

top.name: Microsoft
top.why: Revenue grew +19% on a very large base, with a 49.7% operating margin. Azure grew +48% and RPO reached $677B (+73%). Quarterly capex of $39.4B is the main watch item.

top.name: Palantir
top.why: Revenue rose +96% organically, US commercial +148%. GAAP operating margin was 47% and adjusted FCF margin 53%, and FY26 is guided to +91% (Palantir 8-K). Reliance on government revenue and the difficulty of sustaining this pace keep it at #6.

top.name: Alphabet
top.why: Revenue rose +25% with a 31.8% operating margin, and Cloud grew +103% at a 36% margin. AI capex pushed quarterly FCF to −$9.1B (TTM still +$19.7B), which keeps it out of Tier 1.

top.name: Arista Networks
top.why: Revenue rose +58.5% with no acquisitions, at a 44.9% GAAP operating margin and ~$3.8B of 9-month FCF (Arista 8-K). Concentration in a few large buyers is the flagged risk.

top.name: KLA
top.why: Revenue rose +29% at a 45% GAAP operating margin, the highest in wafer-fab equipment, with TTM FCF of $4.0B. Next quarter is guided ~+14% sequentially (KLA 8-K).

top.name: GE Vernova
top.section: Data-center power, cooling and grid equipment
top.why: Revenue rose +27% (+18% organic) and orders +96% organic. Backlog is $197B and quarterly FCF $5.4B (GE Vernova 8-K). Customer deposits inflate that FCF, and wind still loses money.

top.name: Vertiv
top.section: Data-center power, cooling and grid equipment
top.why: Revenue rose +61% (+55% organic), organic orders more than doubled, GAAP operating margin was 22.8% and adjusted FCF $652M (Vertiv 8-K). It has the most diversified customer base among the AI-hardware names.

top.name: Lam Research
top.why: Revenue rose +54% organically with a 40% GAAP operating margin and $3.24B quarterly FCF (Lam 8-K). China at 35% of revenue and memory-capex cyclicality are the discounts.

top.name: Applied Materials
top.why: Revenue rose +25% with a 33.7% GAAP operating margin and $2.33B FCF, and next quarter is guided ~+12% sequentially (AMAT release). It is solid but grows slower than Lam and KLA.

top.name: Cadence
top.why: Revenue rose +22% with an 85.6% gross margin and 26.2% GAAP operating margin, and backlog reached a record $8.2B (Cadence 8-K). It is one half of the EDA duopoly. $2.14B of 2026 acquisitions blur the organic rate.

top.name: AMD
top.section: Semiconductors: compute, IP and power chips
top.why: Revenue rose +45%, data center +97%, and Q4 is guided at +66%. FCF was only $554M because of inventory build, and GAAP operating margin was 21%.

top.name: Meta Platforms
top.why: Revenue rose +26%, with a 35% operating margin excluding a $9.9B legal charge (20% reported). Quarterly capex of $34.9B drove FCF to −$2.1B.

top.name: Amazon
top.why: AWS grew +39% and backlog is $578B. A 13.9% operating margin and TTM FCF of −$42.4B hold it in the middle.

top.name: Eaton
top.section: Data-center power, cooling and grid equipment
top.why: Revenue rose +28% (+19% organic), segment margin hit a record 25.3% and FCF was $1.03B. The Boyd Thermal acquisition cut gross margin to 34.7% from 38.3% (Eaton 8-K).

top.name: Intuitive Surgical
top.section: Defense tech, robotics and future mobility
top.why: Revenue rose +22%, procedures +15% and the installed base +12%, with a 41.6% non-GAAP operating margin. Its razor/razorblade model makes it the best robotics compounder in the set. GAAP margin (19.4%) absorbed a $450M antitrust charge (Intuitive 8-K).

top.name: CrowdStrike
top.why: Revenue rose +26%, ARR +25% and net new ARR +51%, with a 26% FCF margin and rising retention. GAAP operating margin is still −2.3% (CrowdStrike IR).

top.name: AppLovin
top.why: Revenue rose +55% with a ~78% GAAP operating margin and $1.42B FCF (65%) (AppLovin 8-K). Its financials are top-tier, but ad-tech is less clearly "necessary" in 15 years, and it depends on the Apple and Google platforms.

top.name: Monolithic Power
top.section: Semiconductors: compute, IP and power chips
top.why: Revenue rose +63% organically, gross profit +64% and Enterprise Data +165%, at a 29.7% GAAP operating margin (MPS 8-K). FCF was not disclosed, and revenue is concentrated in AI-GPU power.

top.name: Constellation
top.why: It signed 20-year PPAs with Google and Amazon and earned a 26.1% GAAP operating margin. Its +45% growth is mostly the Calpine acquisition, and 9-month OCF less capex was only $1.5B (Constellation 8-K).

top.name: Micron
top.why: It generated $33.2B of FCF in one quarter and is the only scaled US-headquartered HBM maker. Its 86.8% gross margin is historically unprecedented for memory, so the rank reflects an explicit peak-cycle penalty (Micron 8-K).

top.name: BWX Technologies
top.why: Revenue rose +10% and gross profit +20%. FCF rose +59% to $150.5M and backlog +16% to $8.56B (BWXT 8-K). It is the sole-source naval-reactor supplier and the cleanest profile in nuclear, though growth is slow.

top.name: Datadog
top.why: Revenue rose +35%, NRR is in the low-120s and rising, revenue per customer +29% and FCF margin 21%. The Q4 guide is flat because its largest customer cut usage (Datadog 8-K; sec-api).

top.name: Arm Holdings
top.section: Semiconductors: compute, IP and power chips
top.why: Revenue rose +27% and data-center royalties doubled. Arm holds more than 50% of top-hyperscaler server CPUs (Arm newsroom). GAAP margin is ~14%, FCF was not disclosed, and its move into its own silicon risks conflict with licensees.

top.name: SpaceX
top.why: Revenue rose +161% (~+150% excluding the Cursor acquisition), Starlink reached 13.6M subscribers with ARPU of $69, and operating margin was ~19%. Q3 capex of $19.6B vs $8.8B adj. EBITDA means deep burn, funded by $89.9B of cash and securities (TeslaNorth). This is a long-dated space bet.

top.name: Rocket Lab
top.why: Revenue rose +62% and gross profit +82%, backlog reached $2.36B (+137%), adj. EBITDA was near break-even (−3.8%) and cash is ~$2.39B (Rocket Lab 8-K). It is a high-risk bet on Neutron.

top.name: IonQ
top.why: This is the quantum bet. Platform revenue rose +127%, RPO is $1.2B and pro forma cash is $3.7B (~7-year runway). But 48% of revenue is the acquired SkyWater foundry, and adj. EBITDA was −$133.6M (IonQ release).
